title: net/ib: warn about HCAs that failed to open
body:
## Description

**Problem:** if `ibv_open_device` fails for an IB device on one node (e.g. a container's device cgroup admits only some uverbs devices), that rank has fewer Net devices than the others. With the default `NCCL_IGNORE_NET_MISMATCH=1`, rank 0 logs this only at INFO, other ranks still place channels on their extra devices, and the job can hang after init with no error (#2428).

**Solution:** rank 0 names the device that failed to open:

1. `src/transport/net_ib/init.cc`: record HCAs that fail `ibv_open_device`, with errno, unless excluded by `NCCL_IB_HCA`.
2. `src/init.cc`: share the list and hostname in AllGather3.
3. `src/init.cc`: on a Net device count mismatch, rank 0 prints for each affected rank:
   ```
   NCCL WARN Rank 1 on node-b could not open erdma_1 (ibv_open_device: Permission denied, errno 13). Fix device access or restrict NCCL_IB_HCA.
   ```
   With `NCCL_IGNORE_NET_MISMATCH=1` it adds:
   ```
   NCCL WARN Rank 1: channels on the extra devices of other ranks have no peer here, so the job may hang without an error.
   ```
   With `=0`, the existing error follows as before.

It warns rather than fails, since asymmetric NIC setups can be legitimate. Both lines are WARN (shown with `NCCL_DEBUG=WARN`); happy to switch the ignore-mode lines to `ATTN` if preferred.

**Limitations:**
- Built-in IB transport only; external net plugins are not covered.
- Printed once per affected rank, so multi-GPU nodes repeat it.
- The list is capped at 128 bytes (about two devices).
- The errno is what `ibv_open_device` reports. In containers without `/dev/char`, libibverbs' `open_cdev()` fallback can replace the original error (e.g. `EACCES`) with `ENOENT`. I think keeping the original error belongs in libibverbs rather than NCCL.

## Related Issues

Fixes #2428

## Changes & Impact

- No public API changes or new environment variables.
- Output changes only when counts mismatch and a rank failed to open an allowed device.
- `ncclIbOpenFailedDevs` is also defined in `transport/net_ib_stub.cc` for non-Linux builds (not built here).
- AllGather3 grows by 192 bytes per rank, once per communicator init.

## Performance Impact

None expected; init-time only.

### Testing

2 nodes × 1 L40S, RoCE (mlx5) with GPUDirect RDMA, master (2.32.3), `all_reduce_perf`. Each node has one active port, so rank 0's extra HCA came from a test-only hook (not in this PR).

| Case | Open failure on rank 1 | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `NCCL_IGNORE_NET_MISMATCH=1` | real (`uverbs1` made root-only) | Both WARNs; job runs at full bandwidth |
| `NCCL_IGNORE_NET_MISMATCH=0` | real | Device WARN, then existing error |
| Device excluded via `NCCL_IB_HCA` | simulated | No new WARN |
| Net device counts match | simulated | No new WARN |

The errno-label commit was retested with the simulated cases. The reporter also tested the WARN on eRDMA in a container, which surfaced the errno limitation above.

title: nccl_ep: fix int32 overflow in HT slot offsets
body:
## Description

The hybrid-EP (HT) dispatch/combine JIT kernels in `contrib/nccl_ep/device/hybrid_ep.cuh` compute buffer offsets as `slot_index * stride` with both operands `int32`, then add the product to a typed pointer. The receiver slot space is partitioned by source rank at `max_tokens_per_rank` granularity, so the offset for high sender ranks scales with `rank * max_tokens_per_rank * HIDDEN_DIM` and crosses 2³¹ well within supported configurations:

- With 32 LSA ranks × `max_tokens_per_rank=32768` × `hidden_dim=4096`, the dispatch destination offset goes negative for sender ranks ≥ 16 → deterministic `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in `dispatch_nodes1_lsa32_*` on the upper half of the ranks.
- Observed on a 397B-parameter MoE at TP4/EP32: ranks 20–31 fault, the fault follows the rank index (not the hosts), and is independent of the capacity factor. `max_tokens_per_rank=16384` runs clean with zero margin — `524287 * 4096` is 4 KiB below 2³¹.
- The combine-side read at `slot * HIDDEN_DIM * size_u16<kTokenDtype>()` is in **bytes**, so it overflows at half the token count.
- The local-dup zone write offset scales with the full receive capacity and overflows similarly under large capacity factors.

This PR casts the slot index to `size_t` at every slot-scale multiply: the `dispatch_s2g_issue_token` token/prob/scaling-factor destination pointers, the combine g2s source reads, and the local-dup pad writes.

## Related Issues

<!-- TODO: optionally file an issue with the repro configuration and reference it here -->

## Changes & Impact

No API or behavior change for configurations that previously worked; configurations that previously faulted now address correctly. Header-only changes to the runtime-JIT'd device source — no library binary is affected and the JIT cache re-keys on the new source automatically. Only the slot-scale multiplies that can exceed 2³¹ under currently supported configurations are widened; index arithmetic bounded by per-chunk or per-warp extents remains `int32`.

## Performance Impact

None expected: the widened multiplies are address arithmetic on values already feeding 64-bit pointer additions. Validated in production MoE training (397B parameters, TP4/EP32, GB300) at `max_tokens_per_rank=32768`, where unpatched kernels deterministically fault; throughput at previously-working sizes is unchanged.

title: RFC: External allocator for persistent graph work descriptors
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/pull/2424/files) against `master`.

Related to #2416. This RFC adds a communicator-configured allocator for one audited class: local persistent CUDA Graph work descriptors that do not fit in kernel arguments. It is a scoped prototype, not an implementation of the full external allocator RFE.

The allocator descriptor is copied by value. Paired alloc/free callbacks receive the original byte count and device; allocation receives NCCL's upload stream. Failure propagates without fallback. Plan provenance routes external pointers back to the matching callback. Split communicators inherit the descriptor when no overriding config is supplied. Callback code/context must outlive all graphs, graph executables and communicator destruction, be thread-safe, and must not reenter NCCL.

Transport/exported buffers, registration arenas, NVLS, ordinary enqueue and offload-manager allocations retain their existing paths. Storage remains live throughout graph lifetime. No PyTorch integration or large-model capacity benefit is claimed. The public API and eligibility scope need maintainer agreement.

Validation on upstream 12df1a11afad322be5a204a2db890161cbf8131d, CUDA 12.8, two L20s:
- Clean shared/static build; standalone regression builds with -Wall -Wextra -Werror.
- Six graph captures, three replays each, 64 AllReduce operations per graph with exact outputs.
- Default allocator, legacy config size, missing callback rejection and intentional allocation failure/abort pass.
- External pool and inherited split allocator pass on both enqueue paths, with pointer/size/device validation; 12 allocations and 12 frees, 36,864 bytes per rank.
- The test sets NCCL_WORK_ARGS_BYTES=256 to exercise the persistent path. It does not claim every CUDA failure path has been injected.

Two fresh-process APPA/PAAP quartets, idle L20 GPUs 4/5, CPU affinity 40–47. For each job take the maximum rank mean, then the geometric mean across four jobs per arm. The first graph timing is discarded; each job contributes five capture means and fifteen replays.

| Metric | Baseline default pool µs | External pool µs | Speed change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Capture + instantiate | 151.720 | 138.192 | +9.79% |
| Replay + synchronize (64 AllReduce calls) | 228.083 | 218.724 | +4.28% |

Speed change = baseline/patch − 1. These are descriptive measurements, not a stable speedup claim. Capture job means span 120.841–206.188 µs for baseline and 101.112–173.159 µs for patch on this shared host with unlocked clocks. All patched runs have balanced allocation/free counts. This measures the collective graph lifecycle, not a full training workload.

Reproduction and the standalone regression are in contrib/graph_work_allocator/.

title: Respect explicit device targets for LDMC FP8 compilation
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/pull/2422/files) against `master`.

# B — Explicit LDMC targets

Fixes #2420. Explicit command-line, environment, or pre-included Makefile `NVCC_GENCODE` now controls LDMC FP8 compilation as well. Capture whether the target was supplied before including `common.mk`, and retain toolkit-dependent architecture-specific defaults only when no target was supplied. No generator or target-list parser changes.

Validation on upstream `12df1a11`, CUDA 12.8, NVIDIA L20:

| Check | Baseline | Patch |
|---|---|---|
| Clean `sm_89` shared/static build | PASS | PASS |
| Embedded cubins | `sm_89` + unrequested `sm_100a` | `sm_89` only |
| Shared library size | 77,340,680 bytes | 76,234,784 bytes |
| Immediate shared-library load, `ncclGetVersion` | 23203 | 23203 |
| Whole-archive static consumer | — | PASS |
| Default LDMC target, CUDA 12.8 | `sm_100a` | `sm_100a` |
| Environment target override | ignored by LDMC | `sm_89` |
| Normal/profile LDMC units: `sm_89`, `sm_90`, `sm_100a`, mixed, SASS+PTX | — | 10/10 compiled; inspected cubin/PTX and symbols |
| Four-GPU collective exact correctness | PASS | PASS |
| Two-GPU independent process exact correctness | PASS | PASS |

Runtime comparison on two L20s, 2,097,152 FP32 elements per API count (8 MiB; per peer for AlltoAll), 20 measured iterations after warmup, two independent APPA/PAAP quartets. Wall time includes enqueue and synchronization across ranks. Every output element is checked outside timing.

| Operation | Elements/peer | Baseline µs | Patch µs | Speed change | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| allgather | 2097152 | 1195.43 | 1128.62 | +5.92% | +5.59% |
| allreduce | 2097152 | 1191.05 | 1132.00 | +5.22% | +4.96% |
| alltoall | 2097152 | 943.21 | 915.46 | +3.03% | +2.94% |
| sendrecv | 2097152 | 917.68 | 976.48 | -6.02% | -6.41% |

Speed change is `baseline / patch - 1`; negative values are regressions. These are descriptive runtime checks, not a confirmed speedup claim for this build fix. Earlier four-GPU timings were invalidated after unrelated GPU jobs started and caused large baseline drift; the table uses fresh processes on idle GPUs 6–7, CPU affinity 40–47. No model-serving result is claimed.

Reproduction/build:

```bash
make -j16 src.build CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda \
  NVCC_GENCODE='-gencode=arch=compute_89,code=sm_89' \
  BUILDDIR=/absolute/isolated/build
cuobjdump --list-elf /absolute/isolated/build/lib/libnccl.so
```

CUDA 13.0.2 cross-build (nvcc 13.0.88), with the exact requested target:

```bash
make -j16 src.build CUDA_HOME=/absolute/toolchains/cuda-13.0.2 \
  NVCC_GENCODE='-gencode=arch=compute_121a,code=sm_121a' \
  BUILDDIR=/absolute/isolated/build
```

| CUDA 13 check | Baseline | Patch |
|---|---|---|
| Clean sm_121a shared/static build | PASS | PASS |
| Embedded cubin architectures | sm_100 + sm_121a | sm_121a only |
| Shared library size | 77,490,688 bytes | 77,486,560 bytes |
| Immediate shared load / version | PASS / 23203 | PASS / 23203 |
| Whole-archive static consumer | PASS | PASS |
| Actual LDMC ReduceScatter SASS | sm_100 | sm_121a |

The patched LDMC disassembly contains a real kernel body (1041 disassembly lines), not an empty unsupported-target stub. The official NVIDIA compiler packages were installed in an isolated directory and archive SHA256 checks passed.

This verifies the originally requested target at build/link level. Native GB10/sm_121a execution, aarch64 and CUDA 13.3/13.4 are not tested. L20 runtime checks cover AlltoAll, AllReduce, AllGather and Send/Recv; they do not execute Blackwell LDMC FP8 kernels.

## Send/recv follow-up (2026-09-20)

The earlier -6.02% aggregate is not a reproduced causal regression. Retaining every original sample, the independent quartets disagree:

| Quartet | Baseline geometric mean µs | Patch geometric mean µs | Speed change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| APPA | 917.883 | 1039.982 | -11.74% |
| PAAP | 917.479 | 916.860 | +0.07% |

One patch process measured 1185.101 µs; the other seven processes measured 912.634–921.327 µs. The slow process is retained. Two quartets cannot establish stable improvement, equivalence, or a repeatable regression.

The existing baseline and patch `sendrecv.cu.o` SASS dumps are identical. Host `collectives.o` disassembly differs only in the object filename heading. Follow-up disassembly of the final shared libraries also found identical instruction streams for both `ncclDevKernel_SendRecv` and `ncclDevFunc_SendRecv` on SM89. Both library SHA256 values match the original campaign. This rules out changed instructions in those two GPU functions; it does not explain the slow process or prove equivalent end-to-end timing. No speculative production-code change was made.

The common harness now has an opt-in `perf` mode: 20 warmups, 200 measured iterations, one default-configuration measurement per operation, and the existing exact output checks outside timing. Legacy correctness/trace mode is preserved. `tests/run_b_retest.sh` runs eight APPA/PAAP quartets and refuses selected GPUs with resident compute processes. `tests/summarize_b_retest.py` retains every sample and emits per-quartet and aggregate Markdown tables only for a complete campaign. Formula, blocked-campaign and incomplete-operation checks passed locally. The SM89 retest executable compiled successfully. Its GPU-occupancy gate returned `BLOCKED_BUSY` before launching GPU work.

All eight L20 GPUs had other compute processes during this follow-up. No clean performance rerun has completed, and no performance fix or stable speedup is claimed. Git transport failed, but the GitHub API independently confirmed that current upstream remains `12df1a11afad322be5a204a2db890161cbf8131d`; no rebase changes are needed.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<idle GPU>,<idle GPU> bash tests/run_b_retest.sh
python3 tests/summarize_b_retest.py evidence/b-retest-<timestamp>
```

## Shared-host diagnostic (2026-09-20, GPUs 4–5)

Two fresh-process APPA/PAAP quartets, 20 warmups and 200 timed iterations per operation, 8 MiB API count. All 32 operation results passed exact correctness. GPU 5 had a resident foreign process, so these measurements are diagnostic only and are not clean validation or evidence of a stable speedup. No samples were removed.

| Operation | Baseline µs | Patch µs | Speed change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| alltoall | 923.619 | 908.039 | +1.72% |
| allreduce | 1119.114 | 1142.656 | -2.06% |
| allgather | 1127.519 | 1136.048 | -0.75% |
| sendrecv | 945.928 | 919.607 | +2.86% |

The old send/recv regression did not repeat in this diagnostic. Both baseline and patch still fluctuate. Combined with identical linked send/recv GPU instructions, this does not support a speculative send/recv implementation change. An idle two-GPU campaign remains pending.

## Explicit Makefile target correction (2026-09-20)

The first revision checked `origin NVCC_GENCODE` after including `common.mk`. A caller-supplied Makefile assignment was therefore indistinguishable from a default assignment: requesting SM89 still selected SM100a for LDMC on CUDA 12.8. Capture the origin before including the defaults to respect that explicit target too.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-included Makefile requests SM89, CUDA 12.8 configuration | LDMC incorrectly selects SM100a | LDMC selects SM89 |
| Default, CLI, environment, Makefile × CUDA 12.6/12.8/12.9/13.0 configuration | Makefile override fails | 16/16 PASS |
| CUDA 12.8 native compilation, Makefile SM89 override, normal/profile LDMC units | — | 2/2 PASS; only SM89 cubins |

The 16-case matrix evaluates Make configuration with explicit version values; it is not compilation with four installed CUDA toolkits. This fixes build-target selection and makes no runtime speedup claim. Previous timing measurements apply to the previous revision; this follow-up changes Makefile-defined target selection.

## Runtime-speed investigation (2026-09-20 10:53–10:57)

No runtime performance fix is claimed. A send/recv-only harness preserves exact correctness checking and runs 20 warmups plus 200 measured iterations. The libraries are the same SHA256-verified runtime artifacts as the earlier experiments; the subsequent Makefile-origin correction does not change their explicit command-line compilation flags.

Nsight recorded 440 SendRecv kernel launches per arm. The baseline launch API median was 4.165 µs and the patch median 4.377 µs. GPU kernel duration medians were 1162.717 and 896.409 µs, but maxima reached 17.706 and 32.837 ms. Stream synchronization dominated CUDA API time. These whole-process profiling aggregates include warmup and initialization; they are not a timed-window speed comparison.

Without profiling, four fresh executions of the identical baseline measured 3145.249, 3134.999, 3142.637, and 3135.624 µs. The following APPA/PAAP pair then crossed from approximately 3.15 ms to approximately 0.91 ms mid-campaign:

| Diagnostic quartet | Baseline µs | Patch µs | Speed change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 2671.115 | 3150.783 | -15.22% |
| 1 | 914.289 | 908.654 | +0.62% |

Both quartets are shared-host diagnostics, not clean performance validation. All 14 runs (two profiled, four baseline-only, eight alternating) passed send/recv exact correctness. All samples are retained, including the transition. The direction and magnitude of the difference depend on the changing execution conditions, so these results cannot establish a B-specific slowdown, equivalence, or speedup. The measured code does not justify a speculative SendRecv implementation patch. An idle two-GPU allocation is required to continue causal performance validation.

## Contention correlation audit

The saved GPU process snapshots show two additional foreign compute processes (PIDs 2367650 and 2367651 on GPUs 4 and 5) during the slow quartet. Both are absent before the fast quartet, while the other resident processes remain. No foreign processes were stopped by this task. The intermediate baseline run crosses the transition; snapshots are taken before runs, so their exact exit times are not established.

| Run | Arm | Send/recv µs | Extra GPU 4/5 processes present |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 0-0 | base | 3136.916 | Yes |
| 0-1 | patch | 3153.880 | Yes |
| 0-2 | patch | 3147.689 | Yes |
| 0-3 | base | 2274.481 | Yes |
| 1-0 | patch | 908.292 | No |
| 1-1 | base | 915.707 | No |
| 1-2 | base | 912.873 | No |
| 1-3 | patch | 909.017 | No |

This is evidence of a changed GPU-sharing condition correlated with the timing shift. It strengthens the interference explanation, but is not a controlled causal experiment and does not prove B is performance-neutral. Neither quartet should be used as a clean speedup/regression verdict. The idle-device preflight remains required for formal retesting.

title: fix: preserve NIC sharing across topology trimming
body:
## Description

  With `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` and `NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1`, topology trimming can remove peer GPUs from the graph even though they still share its NICs.

  Recounting GPUs afterward underestimates NIC sharing, affecting AUTO NIC counts and potentially causing multiple GPUs to select the same NIC for GIN connection 0.

  ## Related Issues

  N/A

  ## Changes & Impact

  - Preserve per-NIC GPU sharing counts before topology trimming.
  - Reuse those counts for NET, GIN, and RMA selection.
  - Retain live-path counting during initial topology computation.
  - Add INIT logging for GIN connection-to-device mappings.

  No public API or environment-variable default changes. Existing selection policies are preserved.

  ## Performance Impact

  The fix addresses unbalanced NIC usage caused by losing sharing information during trimming.

title: [Fix] profiler/example: don't dereference a PXN proxy event's foreign context
[Fix] dev_runtime: size GIN signal shadows by the allocated context count
body:
## Problem

`ncclGinDevCommSetup()` rounds the GIN context count up to a multiple of the backend's GIN connection count and publishes the rounded value in `devComm->ginContextCount` (`gin_host.cc`, since 2.31.2). The device indexes the per-context signal shadows with it:

```c
gin->_signalShadows = comm.ginSignalShadows + contextIndex * comm.ginSignalCount;   // gin__funcs.h
```

But `ncclDevrCommCreateInternal()` sizes the shadow region in the resource window before GIN setup runs, using the requested count:

```c
int nGinContexts = reqs->ginContextCount;
...
bufSizeTotal += nGinContexts * ginSignalTotal * sizeof(uint64_t); // include signal shadows
```

Whenever the connection count does not divide the requested context count, contexts in `[requested, rounded)` index past the end of the shadow region. Examples: the default 4 contexts with 3 GIN connections (3 local GIN NICs, `NCCL_GIN_NCONNECTIONS=3`, or `NCCL_GIN_PROXY_NTHREADS=3`) rounds to 6; 1 context with 2 NICs rounds to 2.

NCCL's own device code reaches those contexts:
- `ncclGinBarrierSession` with `ncclGinAllContexts` does `++*shadowPtr` for every context up to `comm.ginContextCount`.
- The symmetric GIN AllGather/ReduceScatter kernels use `blockIdx.x % comm.ginContextCount`.

The overflow is `(rounded - requested) * ginSignalTotal * 8` bytes past the shadow region. It is silent when it lands in the granularity padding of the resource window, and otherwise writes into the next allocation in the symmetric VA space or faults.

## Fix

Compute the shadow size after `ncclGinDevCommSetup()`, using `outDevComm->ginContextCount`. When GIN is not requested, the size is computed exactly as before.

## Testing

I don't have GPUDirect RDMA-capable hardware, so this is verified by code inspection and I could not run it with GIN enabled. Regression testing of the non-GIN paths through the same function, on H200 (both builds from the same tree):
- `docs/examples/06_device_api/01_allreduce_lsa`: PASSED on master and with this PR.
- nccl-tests `all_reduce/all_gather/reduce_scatter_perf -R 2 -c 1` (symmetric kernels, e.g. `AllReduce_RSxLD_AGxST`, which create an internal devComm with a resource window): 0 errors on master and with this PR.

A GIN-enabled run with a context count that the GIN connection count doesn't divide (e.g. `NCCL_GIN_NCONNECTIONS=3`, `ginContextCount=4`, `ncclGinAllContexts` barrier), under compute-sanitizer, would exercise the fixed path directly.

title: [Fix] graph: cap p2p channels by maxCTAs after rounding to a power of 2
body:
## Problem

Fixes #1598.

`ncclTopoComputeP2pChannels()` derives `p2pnChannels` from `nChannels`, which is already capped by `config.maxCTAs` / `NCCL_MAX_CTAS`. It then rounds the value up to a power of 2, which p2p peer-to-channel mapping relies on. When maxCTAs is not a power of 2, the rounded value exceeds it. P2P work is spread over all `p2pnChannels`, and the kernel grid is the number of channels used, so send/recv and all-to-all kernels launch more CTAs than the user allowed. This defeats `maxCTAs` both for reserving SMs for overlapped compute and for limiting per-rank resources with multiple ranks per GPU, which env.rst recommends it for.

As @sjeaugey noted in #1598, `NCCL_MAX_CTAS` should cap the number of channels for all use cases.

## Fix

After the round-up, clamp `p2pnChannels` to `pow2Down(config.maxCTAs)`, so it stays a power of 2 and does not exceed the cap. Also remove the stale comment saying max/minCTAs were already honored there. The default maxCTAs (`MAXCHANNELS`) is a power of 2, so default behavior is unchanged. A p2p channel count below the collective channel count is already a supported state (e.g. `NCCL_MAX_P2P_NCHANNELS=4`).

Tradeoff: with a non-power-of-2 cap, p2p now uses the next lower power of 2 (e.g. 4 channels for `maxCTAs=5`), where master used the next higher one and exceeded the cap. If `minCTAs == maxCTAs` and the value is not a power of 2, p2p ends up below minCTAs; honoring the upper bound seemed the right priority.

This fixes the communicator-level cap. The per-call `ncclAlltoAllConfig` maxCTAs issue (#2421) is separate.

## Testing

4x H200, `alltoall_perf -b 16M -e 16M -t 4 -g 1`. Channel counts are from the INIT log; SendRecv kernel grid sizes are from `nsys` (`cuda_gpu_trace`, GrdX):

| `NCCL_MAX_CTAS` | master: coll / p2p channels, SendRecv grid | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unset | 24 / 32, grid 24–32 | 24 / 32, grid 24–32 (unchanged) |
| 16 | 16 / 16, grid 12–16 | unchanged |
| 6 | 6 / 8, **grid 6–8** | 6 / 4, grid 3–4 |
| 5 | 5 / 8, **grid 6–8** | 5 / 4, grid 3–4 |
| 3 | 3 / 4, **grid 3–4** | 3 / 2, grid 2 |

`alltoall_perf` and `sendrecv_perf -c 1` (8 B – 128 MB) with `NCCL_MAX_CTAS=5` and `3`: 0 errors on master and with this PR.

title: [Fix] net/ib: use ID-based matching whenever receives are pre-posted
body:
## Problem

Pre-posted IB receive work requests all carry `NCCL_IB_RECV_WR_ID_DUMMY` (`UINT64_MAX`) as `wr_id`, so with pre-posting the receiver can only find the request from the ID carried in the immediate data (`BY_ID` matching). The conditions that turn these on are out of sync:

- `ncclIbRecvCommInit()` pre-posts when `NCCL_IB_PREPOST_RECEIVE_WORK_REQUESTS=1`, when OOO RQ is enabled, or when the resiliency context exists. `ncclIbResiliencyInit()` creates it for any non-zero `NCCL_IB_RESILIENCY_PORT_FAILOVER`.
- `ncclIbBaseCommInit()` forces `BY_ID` only for OOO RQ and `NCCL_IB_RESILIENCY_PORT_FAILOVER == 1`.

With `NCCL_IB_PREPOST_RECEIVE_WORK_REQUESTS=1`, or `NCCL_IB_RESILIENCY_PORT_FAILOVER=2`, the receiver stays on index matching and indexes `recvReqs[wc->wr_id]`, i.e. `recvReqs[-1]`. The first receive then fails:

```
NET/IB: Recv comm could not retreive a request found for a successful completion (comm=0x..., wc.wr_id=-1, opcode=129, ...)
... internal error - please report this issue to the NCCL developers
```

## Fix

Force ID-based matching in `ncclIbBaseCommInit()` for every condition that makes the receiver pre-post: OOO RQ, an enabled resiliency context (`baseComm->resiliency`, set just above by `ncclIbResiliencyInit()`), or explicit pre-posting. This runs for both send and recv comms, so the sender switches its immediate data to the request ID as well. The now-unused `extern ncclParamIbResiliencyPortFailover()` declaration is removed.

## Testing

2x H200 on one node, forced onto IB loopback (`NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1`, 1x HDR port). `all_reduce_perf -c 1`, 8 B – 64 MB:

| Setting | master (2.32.3-1) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `NCCL_IB_PREPOST_RECEIVE_WORK_REQUESTS=1` | internal error on first receive | 0 errors |
| `NCCL_IB_RESILIENCY_PORT_FAILOVER=2` | internal error on first receive | 0 errors |
| `NCCL_IB_RESILIENCY_PORT_FAILOVER=1` | 0 errors | 0 errors |
| `NCCL_IB_PREPOST_RECEIVE_WORK_REQUESTS=0` | 0 errors | 0 errors |
| `NCCL_IB_OOO_RQ=0` | 0 errors | 0 errors |

`sendrecv_perf -c 1` with `NCCL_IB_PREPOST_RECEIVE_WORK_REQUESTS=1`: 0 errors with this PR.

title: [Fix] register: return a NULL handle when ncclCommRegister skips a CPU-backed buffer
[Fix] p2p: close the imported SHM segment in CE memcpy mode with cuMem
Honor per-call AlltoAll CTA bounds in P2P plans
body:
Fixes #2421. Preserve the AlltoAll per-call maxCTAs bound when lowering to P2P work, including both enqueue paths. Resolve the existing environment/per-call/communicator precedence before lowering and use a consistent bounded mapping for connection setup, registration, device work and proxy scheduling.

Grouped AlltoAll calls use the tightest cap; ordinary Send/Recv fused into that group shares the cap. Later groups recover the default mapping. Power-of-two channel mapping means maxCTAs=3 can select two channels. Wider collective plans are separated from capped P2P work. Matching caps across ranks are required. This does not implement minCTAs or CTAPolicy.

Validation: clean CUDA 12.8 shared/static SM89 build on upstream 12df1a11afad322be5a204a2db890161cbf8131d, L20. The included MPI regression checks exact output, eager launch grids through CUPTI, captured graph kernel grids, and three real graph replays. Both enqueue paths pass: 2 GPUs with counts 0/1/257/2097152 and 4 GPUs with counts 257/2097152, totaling 576 rank/scenario results. Cases include caps unset/1/3/7, grouped unset/3/1, mixed Send/Recv and AllReduce, and restored defaults. Baseline exceeded caps 1 and 3. Multi-node behavior and the originally reported GB300 are not tested.

Two fresh-process APPA/PAAP quartets on idle L20 GPUs 4/5; CPU affinity 40–47, 20 timed iterations after warmup, exact validation outside timing. Each row is the geometric mean of four process means per arm.

| AlltoAll FP32 elements/peer | maxCTAs | Baseline µs | Patch µs | Speed change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | unset | 23.838 | 23.387 | +1.93% |
| 1 | 1 | 24.213 | 23.391 | +3.51% |
| 1 | 3 | 24.092 | 23.682 | +1.73% |
| 2097152 | unset | 909.798 | 943.074 | -3.53% |
| 2097152 | 1 | 907.386 | 897.637 | +1.09% |
| 2097152 | 3 | 910.555 | 902.809 | +0.86% |

Speed change = baseline/patch − 1. These are descriptive checks, not established speedups: the baseline ignores the cap, and the host is shared with unlocked clocks. The large-message default patch samples include one 1048.871 µs outlier versus approximately 909–911 µs for the other samples. No model E2E performance is claimed.

Reproduction and the standalone test are in contrib/alltoall_config_max_ctas/.

Additional regression: eight fresh 2-GPU MPI jobs (both enqueue paths × eager/graph × counts 257/2097152), 160 rank/scenario results pass exact correctness. The tenth case mixes AlltoAll maxCTAs=1 with AllReduce maxCTAs=7. For 8 MiB it observes separate 1-CTA and 4-CTA kernels in both paths and modes. The harness reports this case's grids without applying a single global cap to the wider AllReduce; the recorded grids were checked separately. This brings the final regression total to 736 rank/scenario results.

title: [Fix] nvls: wire NVLS buffers per channel so a shared parent is not left unset
body:
## Problem

Fixes #2430.

With `splitShare`, a child communicator reuses its parent's NVLS resources and per-channel NVLS peers but can use fewer NVLS channels (e.g. `config.nvlsCTAs`). `ncclNvlsBufferSetup()` runs lazily on the first comm to launch an NVLS collective. It wired only that comm's channels, with that comm's channel count as the buffer stride and allocation size, and then marked the **shared** resources `inited`. If the child ran first, the parent's remaining channels kept NULL buffer pointers, and the parent's next NVLS collective faulted with an illegal memory access.

## Fix

- Size and lay out the NVLS data buffers by the owning comm's channel count (`resources->nChannels`), the same way the credit buffers are already laid out in `ncclNvlsSetup()`. The layout no longer depends on which comm calls setup first.
- Replace `bool inited` with `int nChannelsInited`. Each call wires only the channels in `[nChannelsInited, comm->nvlsChannels)`, so channels that are already in use by another comm are not touched again.

When the parent runs first, the behavior is identical to before: same layout, all channels wired once, and later calls from the child return early.

Tradeoff: if a child runs NVLS first, the shared data buffer is now allocated at the owner's full size (the size the parent would allocate anyway), not the child's smaller size. The MC partition was already reserved at that size.

## Testing

H200 x3 (NVSwitch), CUDA 12.8, driver 580.159.03. Reproducer: one thread per GPU; the child is split with `splitShare=1, nvlsCTAs=N`; 256 MB AllReduce with `NCCL_ALGO=NVLS`; results checked on the host.

| Scenario | master (2.32.3-1) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| child nvlsCTAs=1/2/4/8 first, then parent | illegal memory access (4/4) | PASS (4/4) |
| parent first, then child nvlsCTAs=1/2/4/8/16 | PASS | PASS |
| child nvlsCTAs=16 first | PASS | PASS |
| child(2) → sibling(8) → parent → child | illegal memory access | PASS: wiring grows 0→2→8→16 |
| same matrix with `splitShare=0` | — | PASS (10/10) |

Also ran nccl-tests `all_reduce_perf`, `reduce_scatter_perf` and `all_gather_perf` with `NCCL_ALGO=NVLS -c 1` (8 B – 256 MB): all 0 errors. The change touches only one-time setup, not the data path.

The reproducer source is attached to #2430.

title: graph: size the fused topology XML for all local ranks
body:
## Description

Fixes the "too many XML nodes (max 256)" failure in intra-node topology fusion.

In ncclTopoGetSystem each rank builds its own topology XML in a 256 node buffer, the local ranks exchange them and the result is fused into one tree. The MNNVL path allocates a bigger buffer for the fused tree (nLocalRanks x 256 nodes) but the intra-node path just reused the 256 node per-rank buffer. The fused tree is the union of all local trees though. Nodes only dedup when every attribute matches and the gpu node carries a per-rank "rank" attribute, so each rank's gpu subtree gets appended, plus anything else that differs per rank. On big hosts this goes past 256 and xmlAddTree fails, so ncclCommInitRank returns ncclInternalError.

This just makes the enlargement unconditional, same thing the MNNVL path already did.

## Related Issues

Fixes #2160

## Changes & Impact

One place in src/graph/topo.cc. The fused xml is now always allocated with nLocalRanks x NCCL_TOPO_XML_MAX_NODES nodes. The MNNVL path is unchanged in behavior, the intra-node path gets the same buffer size.

Tested on one GPU (RTX 2070) with several ranks on the same device (NCCL_MULTI_RANK_GPU_ENABLE=1) and a topology file that gives the gpu 18 nvlink children, so each rank contributes 19 nodes that cannot dedup: 12 ranks fuse to 233 nodes and pass, 14 ranks (271 nodes) fail before this change and pass after it. The fused NCCL_TOPO_DUMP_FILE output for 2 and 8 ranks is byte identical before and after. all_reduce_perf with -c 1 passes. Built with WERROR=1 and checked with an ASAN build. I could not test on a real multi GPU host, MNNVL, or with the EFA/IB plugins.

Out of scope: the 256 node limit when loading a topology file (NCCL_TOPO_FILE) is unchanged, and the warning text is the same.

## Performance Impact

Init only. The fused xml is freed at the end of ncclTopoGetSystem, so it is a transient host allocation of about 3.6 MB per local rank (8 GPUs: ~29 MB per process for the duration of topology detection). No change to the data path.

title: net/ib: stop each Qp profiler event exactly once
body:
## Description

net_ib stops a request's Qp profiler events from two paths, so in the common success path the same event is stopped twice. The profiler API requires each event to be stopped exactly once. The profilers in this repo happen to tolerate the extra stop, so the bug is silent here. But a custom profiler that does real work on stop — free/recycle the handle, decrement a refcount, close a span — will double-free or crash. This PR makes the stop idempotent.

**Problem:** `ncclIbCompletionEventProcess` stops a Qp when its successful CQE is
reaped; `ncclIbRequestComplete` then unconditionally stops all of the request's
Qp events (a safety net for error/resiliency completions never stopped by the
per-completion path). In the success path both run, so each reaped Qp is stopped
twice.

**Solution:** add `ncclIbStopQpEvent()`, which stops an event only if its handle
is non-NULL and then clears the handle, making any later stop a no-op. Route all
four stop sites through it, keeping the request-complete safety net.

## Reproduction

1. Build with net profiling: `make NET_PROFILER=1`.
2. In a profiler plugin, enable the `ncclProfileNetPlugin` bit and count each
   NetPlugin `startEvent`/`stopEvent`.
3. Run over the in-tree IB transport: `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none NCCL_NET=IB`.

Without the fix, stops exceed starts (double-stopped Qps); with the fix they are
balanced 1:1.

## Related Issues

N/A

## Changes & Impact

Single file `src/transport/net_ib/p2p.cc`: adds a `static inline` helper and
routes the four Qp `stopEvent` sites through it. No public API/ABI or data-path
change; all new code is under `#ifdef NCCL_ENABLE_NET_PROFILING`, so default
builds are unaffected.

## Performance Impact

None — only a NULL check and pointer clear per Qp `stopEvent`, and only when
built with `NET_PROFILER=1`.

title: device: fix single-node NVLS AllGather/ReduceScatter rank ordering (#1906)
body:
Fixes #1906.

## The bug

Single-node NVLS AllGather returns each rank's chunk in the **wrong output position** when `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` permutes GPUs out of dense-head order — a silent data corruption (the output is a permutation of the correct result). @sjeaugey confirmed the root cause on the issue: the single-node NVLS AllGather is *"missing the user rank table which ensures proper data ordering."*

In the non-registered `oneNode` path:

```
src/device/all_gather.h:     prims.gather(offset, nvls->nHeads * count, nelem, count, -1, 0);
  ⟶ src/device/prims_simple.h (ScatterGatherOp, Recv branch):  pOffset = i * peerOffset;
```

the peer loop index `i` is the **dense head index**, so head `i`'s gathered slice is written to output slot `i`. But head `i` physically holds the data of user rank `denseToUserRank[i]`, so slot `i` is wrong whenever `denseToUserRank[i] != i`.

Every correct sibling path already remaps through `denseToUserRank`:

- multi-node NVLS — `all_gather.h:317`: `int rank = denseToUserRank[node*nRails+rail]; userOneBeg = rank*countPerRank;`
- CollNetDirect — `all_gather.h:546` (same form)
- the PAT helper `nvlsDenseToUserOffset` in `prims_simple.h`

`ReduceScatter` has the exact symmetric mirror (`reduce_scatter.h`, `oneNode`/`!regUsed` scatter → `pOffset = i*peerOffset` on the *source* side). The `oneNode` **`regUsed`** paths use `rank*count` directly and are already correct; multi-node paths are already correct; and `AllReduce`'s NVLS scatter+gather round-trip is order-invariant (its output is the fully-reduced array), so it must **not** change.

## Why this is device-only

The `denseToUserRank` table is already **built and copied to the device for pure single-node NVLS** on current master — `ncclTransportInitRankMap` (`init.cc:1573`) is gated only on `comm->nvlsSupport` (no `nNodes>1` guard), and `devCommSetup` copies it (`init.cc:698`, null-guarded). So no host / `comm.h` / `init.cc` / `connect.cc` changes are needed — only the device-side consumption was missing.

## The fix

- `ScatterGatherOp` gains an opt-in `template <..., bool Remap = false>` plus a `const int* remap = nullptr`; the per-peer offset becomes `(Remap && remap != nullptr) ? remap[i] : i`. Because `Remap` is a template constant, **every existing caller compiles to byte-identical code** (AllReduce, multi-node, CollNet, the two reg-sync `gather/scatter(0,0,0,0,-1,0)`, `directScatter`/`directGather`) — they don't pass the new arg.
- New `scatterRemap()` / `gatherRemap()` wrappers set `Remap=true`.
- The two `oneNode` NVLS sites pass `ncclShmem.comm.denseToUserRank`, so peer `i`'s slice is placed at slot `denseToUserRank[i]` — matching the multi-node/CollNet/PAT direction exactly.

## Direction (the load-bearing detail)

Specialized to a single node (`node=0`, `nRails=nHeads`), the correct multi-node formula `rank = denseToUserRank[node*nRails+rail]; slot = rank*count` reduces to `slot(i) = denseToUserRank[i]`. `denseToUserRank[i]` is the user rank that owns head `i` (`generic.cc` builds `userToDenseRank` then inverts it; for a head rank `r`, `userToDenseRank[r]=h` where `nvlsHeads[h]==r`). So peer `i` (head `i`) → output slot `denseToUserRank[i]`. Using the inverse table would double-permute; this uses the same table and direction as every correct path.

## Testing

I **cannot validate this on hardware** — I don't have an NVSwitch box and can't do a full NCCL build. I verified: (1) the fix matches the multi-node / CollNet / PAT remap direction line-for-line; (2) the C++ template/overload/wrapper mechanics compile clean and a standalone harness confirms `scatterRemap`/`gatherRemap` permute the per-peer offset by `remap[]` and that an identity remap is byte-identical to plain `scatter`/`gather`.

Please validate on NVSwitch before merging — I'd suggest `all_gather_perf` / `reduce_scatter_perf` forcing `NCCL_ALGO=NVLS`, with `#wrong == 0` across the identity and several non-identity `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` permutations (e.g. `1,2,3,4,5,6,7,0` and `3,4,5,6,7,0,1,2`), plus a non-NVLS regression pass.

Two notes for reviewers: the `ReduceScatter` change is the symmetric mirror (the issue reproduces AllGather only — happy to drop it if you'd rather land AllGather first), and both sites keep the existing `nvls->nHeads*count` span, which assumes `nHeads == nRanks` on this single-node path (as the current code already does).

Disclosure: this contribution was authored with an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed before submission.

title: transport: agree on cuMem host buffers with the peer
body:
## Description

Since 2.26.3 every process probes whether cuMem host allocations work (`ncclCuMemHostEnable`) and falls back to `/dev/shm` when they do not. In the SHM transport the rank that allocates a buffer picks the kind from its own probe result, and the rank that imports it branches on *its* own probe result rather than on the descriptor's `legacy` flag. If the probe passes on one rank and fails on another, the fallback rank reads the cuMem handle bytes through the `/dev/shm` half of the `shmIpcDesc` union: the handle value becomes the file name and the zeroed tail becomes the size, which is exactly the reported `Error while attaching to shared memory segment /dev/shm/nccl-<garbage> (size 0)`. The analysis in the issue shows how the driver can reject `cuMemCreate(HOST_NUMA)` on some NUMA nodes but not others; any other reason for the probe to diverge produces the same failure.

This adds the cuMem host capability to `ncclPeerInfo`, next to the existing `cuMemSupport`, and requests a legacy `/dev/shm` segment whenever either side of a connection lacks it. The same rule is applied at the three places that allocate a host buffer for another process to import: the SHM transport (`shmSendSetup`/`shmRecvSetup`), the PXN shared buffer created by the proxy rank in the net transport (`netCreateShm`), and the P2P copy-engine path (`p2pSendProxySetup` with `NCCL_P2P_USE_CUDA_MEMCPY=1`). A rank that can use cuMem can always open a `/dev/shm` segment (that direction already works today), so mixed nodes now initialize. Pairs where both ranks can use cuMem host memory keep using it. The importer additionally refuses a cuMem descriptor it cannot decode with a clear message instead of trying a garbage path.

## Related Issues

Fixes #2190

## Changes & Impact

Five files, about 30 lines: `src/include/transport.h` (new `int cuMemHostSupport` in the internal `ncclPeerInfo`, exchanged at init like the other fields), `src/init.cc` (`fillInfo` sets it from `ncclCuMemEnable() && ncclCuMemHostEnable()`, the same predicate the allocator uses), `src/transport/shm.cc` (the `req.legacy` decision in both setup functions, plus the importer check), `src/transport/net.cc` (`setupReq.shmLegacy` computed in `sendSetup` from the importing rank and the proxy rank, carried to `netCreateShm`), `src/transport/p2p.cc` (`ncclP2pRequest.shmLegacy`; the CE branch of `p2pSendSetup` now sends the request it already builds). No public API or ABI change; no data-path change.

Tested on one GPU with two processes that rendezvous through `NCCL_COMM_ID` and use the SHM transport, with `NCCL_CUMEM_HOST_ENABLE` set to 1 in one process and 0 in the other: before, the rank set to 0 fails with the exact message from the issue in both directions of the mismatch; after, both directions initialize, complete an all-reduce, and log `MMAP imported` on both sides. Both matching configurations behave as before (`CUMEM`/`MMAP` unchanged). Also run: `all_reduce_perf -g 1 -c 1`, an in-process two-rank all-reduce over P2P and over SHM (same-process pairs still use the legacy segment), `WERROR=1` build, `DEBUG=1 ASAN=1` build through the reproducer. Not tested: multi-GPU PCIe nodes where SHM is chosen naturally (two ranks on one GPU are at PATH_LOC distance and always take P2P, so a local test hook was needed to force SHM), the PXN path (no NIC here) and the CE path (its per-communicator proxy pool does not fit twice in this container's 64 MB `/dev/shm`), fabric handle types, Windows.

Note, out of scope: the probe runs once per process for the device current on first call, so a single process driving GPUs on several NUMA nodes still applies one node's answer to all of them.

## Performance Impact

None on the data path. One call to a cached function per rank at init. Connections involving a rank that cannot use cuMem host memory use `/dev/shm`, which is what that rank already did for its own buffers.

title: Fix typo in ibverbs dlopen failure message

title: graph/os: close the topology file and sysfs directory on error paths
body:
## Problem

Four error paths return with an open handle:

- `ncclTopoDumpXmlToFile`, `ncclTopoGetXmlFromFile`, `ncclTopoGetXmlGraphFromFile` (`src/graph/xml.cc`): each `fopen`s the topology/graph file and then `NCCLCHECK`s the XML dump/parse **before** `fclose`, so a failure — e.g. a malformed `NCCL_TOPO_FILE` / `NCCL_GRAPH_FILE` — returns with the `FILE*` leaked (and, for the dump, unflushed).
- `ncclOsGetBcmLinks` (`src/os/linux.cc`): `opendir`s the Broadcom switch link directory and `NCCLCHECK`s the peers `ncclRealloc` inside the `readdir` loop, returning without `closedir` if it fails.

## Fix

- xml.cc: capture the result, `fclose`, then `NCCLCHECK(res)` — the same shape as the fd fixes in #2267 / #2376.
- linux.cc: `ncclResult_t ret`, `NCCLCHECKGOTO(..., ret, exit)` and an `exit:` label just before `closedir(dir)` inside the same `if (dir)` block, returning `ret`.

No behaviour change on the success paths.

I don't have a CUDA build environment here, so this was checked by inspection plus an independent review pass (goto legality, double close, semantic change).

Disclosure: this contribution was authored with an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed before submission.

title: RAS: fix use-after-free in rasMsgHandlePeersUpdate
body:
## Problem

`rasMsgHandlePeersUpdate()` merges a received `RAS_MSG_PEERSUPDATE` into the local peer/dead-peer tables. For every *newly* dead peer in the message, `rasDeadPeersUpdate()` calls `rasConnDisconnect()`, which terminates the connection and frees both the `rasConnection` and **all of its sockets** — including, possibly, the very socket the message is being received on.

If the message's `deadPeers` list contains the address of the peer it was received from, the handler frees its own connection/socket mid-processing and then keeps dereferencing `sock->conn`:

- reads at `src/ras/peers.cc` (`conn->lastSentPeersHash` / `lastRecvPeersHash` etc.),
- writes (`conn->lastSentDeadPeersHash = ...`),
- `rasConnEnqueueMsg()` into the freed connection's send queue.

This is a use-after-free on the RAS thread, which shares the address space of the training process, so a crash takes down the rank. Two properties make this worse than a rare race:

1. **No race is required.** The sender fully controls the `deadPeers` payload; a faulty (or malicious) peer can deterministically trigger the UAF on a neighbor by including its own address.
2. **It can be hit organically at scale.** When a peer is declared dead prematurely (e.g., a keepalive timeout false positive under load), it merges its own "death" and propagates the full `rasDeadPeers` array over its still-live links before exiting — delivering exactly the triggering message to its ring neighbors.

We originally root-caused this after a production training job crashed with a RAS thread segfault whose signature resembled the case-2 report in #1996; with this fix applied, the crash no longer reproduces.

## Root cause

```
rasMsgHandlePeersUpdate            src/ras/peers.cc   (sock->conn used after merge)
  -> rasDeadPeersUpdate            src/ras/peers.cc   (rasConnDisconnect on newly dead)
    -> rasConnDisconnect           src/ras/rasnet.cc
      -> rasConnTerminate          src/ras/rasnet.cc  (frees conn)
        -> rasSocketTerminate(..., finalize=true)     (frees every sock with sock->conn == conn)
```

Note that the event loop caller is already prepared for handlers terminating sockets (`rasSockEventLoop()` re-checks `rasPfds[].revents` after `rasMsgHandle()`), and `rasMsgHandleConnInitAck()` explicitly copies the address "because rasConnDisconnect will terminate the rasSocket" — the peers-update path was simply missing this protection.

## Evidence

AddressSanitizer, harness compiling the real `src/ras/peers.cc` + `src/ras/rasnet.cc` with stubbed socket I/O (no multi-node setup needed):

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free
READ of size 8 ... rasMsgHandlePeersUpdate      src/ras/peers.cc:609
freed by ... freeSockEntry                       src/ras/rasnet.cc:429
             rasSocketTerminate                  src/ras/rasnet.cc:578
             rasConnTerminate                    src/ras/rasnet.cc:345
             rasConnDisconnect                   src/ras/rasnet.cc:336
             rasDeadPeersUpdate                  src/ras/peers.cc:873
             rasMsgHandlePeersUpdate             src/ras/peers.cc:593
```

## Fix

In `rasMsgHandlePeersUpdate()`:

- save the connection and a copy of its address *before* the dead-peer merge;
- after `rasDeadPeersUpdate()`, if the sender is now in the dead set, drop the connection reference (otherwise re-validate it with `rasConnFind()`), so the freed connection/socket is never touched again;
- newly learned dead peers are still propagated to the remaining RAS links (`rasNetUpdatePeers(..., fromConn=nullptr)`), so dead-peer dissemination is not delayed.

The normal path (sender not in the dead set) is byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged.

## Testing

- ASan reproducer, "self" mode (dead peer == sender): heap-use-after-free before the fix; clean pass after.
- ASan reproducer, "other" mode (dead peer is a third party): passes before and after — no regression on the normal path.
- File formatted with clang-format 22 per the repo's `.clang-format`; `maint/run-clang-format.sh --diff` reports no changes.

title: enqueue: clamp NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE to the P2P step size
body:
## Description

Fixes wrong ncclSend/ncclRecv data and GPU memory faults when NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE is set larger than the P2P step size.

The P2P kernels move one chunk per step into a buffer slot that is stepSize bytes (comm->p2pChunkSize for the simple protocol, the LL buffer divided by NCCL_STEPS for LL). addP2pToPlan applies NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE to the chunk without checking it against that step, so a larger value makes the kernel write past its slot: it overwrites the neighbouring slots that are still in flight (wrong values) and, from the last slot, runs past the end of the buffer (illegal memory access, or an Xid 31 read fault on a GPUDirect registered network buffer). On a socket network the receiver posts a step sized receive and the sender ships the chunk, so the plugin logs "message truncated" and the kernel waits forever.

This clamps the chunk to the step size and prints a warning once (simple protocol only, the LL clamp never changes anything in practice), saying which variables actually raise the step (NCCL_BUFFSIZE together with NCCL_P2P_NET_CHUNKSIZE / NCCL_P2P_PCI_CHUNKSIZE / NCCL_P2P_NVL_CHUNKSIZE). That is the same thing computeBuffSizes already does silently for p2pChunkSize itself. While at it, values at or below zero are ignored and the chunk gets a 16 byte floor: a negative value used to encode to a huge chunk and NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE=1 crashed with a division by zero on the LL path.

## Related Issues

Fixes #2408. Same symptom as the older #1496.

## Changes & Impact

One block in src/enqueue/enqueue.cc (addP2pToPlan), 12 added lines, 2 changed. Only NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE users are affected. Values up to the step size behave as before. Values above it now get the step size plus one warning per process instead of corrupt data. That includes values that happened to work on PCIe/SHM systems because the physical slot there (buffer / NCCL_STEPS) is bigger than the step; those users will see a smaller chunk than before (about 12% less send/recv bandwidth for 256K on my PCIe host) and the warning tells them how to get a bigger one properly.

Tested on one host with two GPUs (RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 2070, no P2P, SHM transport, and NET/Socket with P2P and SHM disabled) with a small two rank send/recv program that checks every byte: without the patch a 1 MiB chunk over the 128 KiB step gives an illegal memory access on SHM, any chunk above the step hangs on NET/Socket after the "message truncated" warning, and two ranks on one GPU with a 4 MiB chunk get wrong bytes. With the patch all cases pass, and sendrecv_perf / alltoall_perf -g 2 -c 1 with NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE=1M, 256K and unset report 0 wrong values. Built with WERROR=1. I could not test IB/RoCE with GPUDirect (the reporter's setup), NVLink or multi node.

Out of scope: making bigger chunks actually work (bigger buffers / steps, what the reporter really wants for bandwidth) is a design change; and the docs still describe NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE as a bandwidth knob (happy to add a sentence about the clamp to performance_and_tuning.rst if you want it in this PR).

## Performance Impact

None on the data path. One extra comparison per P2P task at plan time. Users who set NCCL_CHUNK_SIZE above the step size get the step sized chunk, which is what the buffers can carry anyway.
